sourceFacts: Supported knee sliding precedes the outbound knee-hover/knee-down return.
Controlled elbow sequence, head height and glute engagement are teaching priorities.
appDecisions: Opt-in block and eligible basic ABC support
2–4 sets of 3, 60-second rests, planning seconds and freshness/exposure gates

kneeSlidingPlank.purpose: Develop controlled core engagement while moving between child-position reach and knee-supported low-plank positions.
setup: Use a clear, comfortable surface for hands, elbows and knees. Begin standing and lower under control.
Find hand distance with a comfortable child-position reach; start the supported version with knees and tops of feet down.
steps: Slide forward with eyes toward the floor and a controlled, nearly constant head height.
Let the elbows touch and then lift as hands come beneath shoulders, keeping elbows close.
At extension, engage the glutes, tuck the tailbone and keep the abdomen engaged.
Reverse with elbow contact, then straighten the arms in the rear position. Return to standing with control when finished.
bracing: Exhale at the front where the greatest tension is sought; maintain glute and abdominal engagement.
mistakes: Rising and falling instead of sliding at controlled height: slow down and return to supported range.
Omitting the glute squeeze or flaring elbows: reduce the demand and rehearse the sequence.

qualifications: The captions include an inconsistent toe cue. This lesson follows the explicitly described initial supported setup, while the toe-tucked knee-hover progression is distinguished in #94.
The app selects 2–4 sets of 3 reps and 60-second rest as practice defaults; #86 does not prescribe those numbers.

hoverSlidingPlank.purpose: Extend the supported sliding plank by hovering the knees on the outbound portion, then lowering them for the return.
setup: Confirm the supported sliding pattern first. Use comfortable low kneeling and reach out to establish hand distance.
Tuck toes and push back with the arms so the knees lift slightly without forcing range.
steps: From the rear hover, touch elbows and slide forward under control.
At extension, keep elbows close, engage glutes and tuck the tailbone.
Without collapsing the trunk, place the knees down and return through elbow contact.
bracing: Retain the earlier trunk and glute engagement; the hover adds complexity rather than permission to lose alignment.
mistakes: Rushing and missing the knee-down return: rehearse slowly or use the supported version.
Sagging at extension: reduce demand and regain the basic sequence.

qualifications: Knee-hover height and depth are individual technique context, not an automatic target.
